instructions: Pat the cutlets dry. If any are thicker than 1/2 inch, pound them with a rolling pin or the bottom of a heavy pan until they are about 1/2 inch thick.
Put the flour on a plate. Season both sides of the cutlets with 1/2 tsp of the salt and 1/4 tsp of the pepper. Press each cutlet into the flour and shake off the extra.
Slice the mozzarella into thin rounds and set them on a paper towel. Tear 8 to 10 basil leaves and set them aside.

Heat 1 tbsp of the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat until it shimmers. Add half the cutlets and cook for 2 minutes, until the underside is golden. Flip them and cook for 1 minute. Transfer them to a plate.
Add 1 tbsp of oil to the pan and cook the rest of the cutlets the same way. They will finish cooking in the sauce.
Lower the heat to medium and add the last tbsp of oil. Add the garlic and stir for 30 seconds, until it smells sweet. Don't let it brown.
Add the oregano and stir for 10 seconds. Add the tomato purée, the remaining 1/2 tsp salt and the remaining 1/4 tsp pepper. If it's very thick, add a splash of water.
Bring the sauce to a simmer, scraping up the browned bits from the bottom of the pan. Simmer for 3 minutes.

Return the cutlets to the pan with any juices and spoon some sauce over them. Cover and simmer gently for 5 minutes. You're cooking the chicken to 160°F in the middle, so if you have a thermometer, check it there. No thermometer? Cut into the thickest cutlet: it's done when there's no pink left.
Lay the mozzarella over the cutlets, cover, and cook for 2 minutes, until it melts.
Take the pan off the heat and scatter the torn basil over the top.
Taste the sauce. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt. Serve with crusty bread or buttered pasta.
method_notes: Honest time is 30 minutes using thin-sliced cutlets from the store; if you slice whole breasts yourself, add about 5 minutes. All three sources agree on the method: a quick sear, then the chicken finishes in a tomato sauce built on garlic and dried oregano, with mozzarella melted on top at the end. They differ on extras (capers and chili flakes in one, a breaded cutlet and a longer-simmered sauce in another); I followed the lead, kept the base mild, and left out the capers. Ratings come from the visible rating on each page, since the page text did not show the JSON-LD.
